name: IBBIS (International Biosecurity and Biosafety Initiative for Science)
summary: A Geneva-based Swiss foundation, incubated by NTI | bio and launched in 2024, that works to keep DNA synthesis from being used to make dangerous pathogens: commec, a free open-source tool synthesis providers use to screen orders, a screening evaluation portal run with NIST, customer-screening resources, two expert consortia on screening standards and sequences of concern, the Global DNA Synthesis Map, policy engagement in the EU, UK and US, and in-country workshops. It publishes no accounts.

spending.source: https://ibbis.bio/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Annual-Letter-Executive-Director-1.pdf (no accounts or budget are published: our estimate from its staff, about 7.5 core staff on average in 2025 (doubled to a full-time team of 10 by the year's end, the annual letter) and 1 fellow (60% of whose time it pays), at the shared cost of a work-year ($250,000, overheads included) × 1.2 for events and grants)

lines.label: Screening tools, standards consortia, the synthesis map, policy engagement and workshops (every programme)
lines.source: https://ibbis.bio/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Annual-Letter-Executive-Director-1.pdf (IBBIS publishes no split of its spending; one line because charityevals models all its work as pandemic field work in one catastrophic-risk model)
